name: Samuel
charge: Speak, Lord; for thy servant heareth: telling Eli every whit and hiding nothing; and an accounting no man could contradict, whose ox have I taken?
summary: Given to the Lord as a child, he served before Eli in days when the word of the Lord was precious and visions were rare. The Lord came and stood and called him by name, and the child did not yet know the Lord until Eli taught him how to answer. His first test as a judge was to carry a judgment against the house that raised him, and he told Eli all of it and held nothing back. The Lord made every one of his words come to pass; he judged Israel all the days of his life, established the kingdom, and by his faithfulness was found a true prophet.
offenseFull: The child Samuel served the Lord under Eli when the word of the Lord was precious and visions were rare (1 Samuel 3:8-14). Precious means the Lord was not dealing with everybody; not with the priests, and there were no prophets around saying what the Lord had spoken. Twice the Lord called and the child ran to Eli, because Samuel did not yet know the Lord. He had been in the house of the Lord since he was weaned, and he still did not know the Lord. That goes in on those playing church with their children: just because your children come and sit and listen does not mean they know the Lord; they are there because you brought them. Your job is the training, raising a child in the path he should keep (Proverbs 22:6); the revealing belongs to the Most High, for only the Son knows the Father, and He reveals Him to whom He chooses (Matthew 11:27). The third time Eli understood, and taught the child to answer that the Lord’s servant was listening.

The Lord came and stood and called as before, Samuel, Samuel. He did not simply call out of the heavens; He came down and stood by him. Samuel could not see Him, but he heard Him, and that is what happens in the spirit to all of us. The Lord is merciful with us even in this wickedness, standing at the door and knocking, calling numerous times until we wake up (Revelation 3:20). Those who heed His correction receive His spirit and His words; those who refuse, and the day comes when they call and He will not answer (Proverbs 1:23). The word given to the child was a judgment against the house that raised him: Eli’s house judged for ever, its sin beyond the reach of any sacrifice. When the Lord is angry, He is angry; do not sin a sin so great that it cannot be prayed for.

In the morning Samuel was afraid to tell Eli the vision, but Eli charged him to hide nothing, and Samuel told him all of it (1 Samuel 3:18-21). He was going to be a judge of Israel, and this was his first test: do not sugarcoat what the Lord has said, and do not trim your words to seek love. Years later he put his own record before the nation, and the people agreed he had taken nothing from anyone (1 Samuel 12:3-4). Nor did he abandon them: he would count it a sin against the Lord to stop praying for them, and he would keep teaching them the good and right way (1 Samuel 12:23). Marinate on that. For a leader of Israel, ceasing to pray for the nation is itself a transgression.
judgmentFull: Samuel grew, and the Lord was with him. What Samuel said, it came to pass. All Israel from Dan to Beersheba knew he was confirmed as a prophet of the Lord (1 Samuel 3:18-21). At Mizpeh he told Israel that if they were returning to the Lord with all their hearts they must get rid of the foreign gods and the Ashtaroth and serve Him only, and they did (1 Samuel 7:3-6). That is repentance. When the Philistine lords came up and Israel was afraid, this time the people did not run for the ark; they begged Samuel not to stop crying to the Lord for them, because they knew the earnest prayer of a righteous man is powerful and effective (James 5:16).

Samuel offered a lamb and cried to the Lord for Israel, and as the Philistines closed in, the Lord thundered against them and routed them (1 Samuel 7:8-13). That was no regular thunder; that was the Lord entering the battle Himself.

They had repented and put away the false gods, and the prayer of a righteous man reached His ears. Samuel set up a stone and named it Ebenezer, and the Philistines were held back all his days. He judged Israel all his life, circling each year through Bethel, Gilgal and Mizpeh and home to Ramah (1 Samuel 7:15-17). That yearly circuit is leadership making its rounds, establishing the people and coming back to check on them, as Paul went back to visit the brethren in every city (Acts 15:36). Ecclesiasticus remembers him as beloved of his Lord, proved a true prophet by his faithfulness (Ecclesiasticus 46:13-15). Faithfulness translates loyalty. He came up under Eli, watched Eli’s sons go wicked, watched Eli die and the nation take losses, and stayed loyal to the Most High. Prayer is a superpower, and that is how our forefathers rolled, from Moses to Samuel all the way to Christ. What was written before was written to teach us (Romans 15:4).

text.text: And the Lord called Samuel again the third time. And he arose and went to Eli, and said, Here am I; for thou didst call me. And Eli perceived that the Lord had called the child.
Therefore Eli said unto Samuel, Go, lie down: and it shall be, if he call thee, that thou shalt say, Speak, Lord; for thy servant heareth. So Samuel went and lay down in his place.
And the Lord came, and stood, and called as at other times, Samuel, Samuel. Then Samuel answered, Speak; for thy servant heareth.
And the Lord said to Samuel, Behold, I will do a thing in Israel, at which both the ears of every one that heareth it shall tingle.
In that day I will perform against Eli all things which I have spoken concerning his house: when I begin, I will also make an end.
For I have told him that I will judge his house for ever for the iniquity which he knoweth; because his sons made themselves vile, and he restrained them not.
And therefore I have sworn unto the house of Eli, that the iniquity of Eli’s house shall not be purged with sacrifice nor offering for ever.
Train up a child in the way he should go: and when he is old, he will not depart from it.
All things are delivered unto me of my Father: and no man knoweth the Son, but the Father; neither knoweth any man the Father, save the Son, and he to whomsoever the Son will reveal him.
Behold, I stand at the door, and knock: if any man hear my voice, and open the door, I will come in to him, and will sup with him, and he with me.
Turn you at my reproof: behold, I will pour out my spirit unto you, I will make known my words unto you.
And Samuel told him every whit, and hid nothing from him. And he said, It is the Lord: let him do what seemeth him good.
And Samuel grew, and the Lord was with him, and did let none of his words fall to the ground.
And all Israel from Dan even to Beer–sheba knew that Samuel was established to be a prophet of the Lord.
And the Lord appeared again in Shiloh: for the Lord revealed himself to Samuel in Shiloh by the word of the Lord.

Behold, here I am: witness against me before the Lord, and before his anointed: whose ox have I taken? or whose ass have I taken? or whom have I defrauded? whom have I oppressed? or of whose hand have I received any bribe to blind mine eyes therewith? and I will restore it you.
And they said, Thou hast not defrauded us, nor oppressed us, neither hast thou taken ought of any man’s hand.
Moreover as for me, God forbid that I should sin against the Lord in ceasing to pray for you: but I will teach you the good and the right way:

And Samuel spake unto all the house of Israel, saying, If ye do return unto the Lord with all your hearts, then put away the strange gods and Ashtaroth from among you, and prepare your hearts unto the Lord, and serve him only: and he will deliver you out of the hand of the Philistines.
Then the children of Israel did put away Baalim and Ashtaroth, and served the Lord only.
And Samuel said, Gather all Israel to Mizpeh, and I will pray for you unto the Lord.

And they gathered together to Mizpeh, and drew water, and poured it out before the Lord, and fasted on that day, and said there, We have sinned against the Lord. And Samuel judged the children of Israel in Mizpeh.
Confess your faults one to another, and pray one for another, that ye may be healed. The effectual fervent prayer of a righteous man availeth much.
And the children of Israel said to Samuel, Cease not to cry unto the Lord our God for us, that he will save us out of the hand of the Philistines.
And Samuel took a sucking lamb, and offered it for a burnt offering wholly unto the Lord: and Samuel cried unto the Lord for Israel; and the Lord heard him.

And as Samuel was offering up the burnt offering, the Philistines drew near to battle against Israel: but the Lord thundered with a great thunder on that day upon the Philistines, and discomfited them; and they were smitten before Israel.
And the men of Israel went out of Mizpeh, and pursued the Philistines, and smote them, until they came under Beth–car.
Then Samuel took a stone, and set it between Mizpeh and Shen, and called the name of it Eben–ezer, saying, Hitherto hath the Lord helped us.
So the Philistines were subdued, and they came no more into the coast of Israel: and the hand of the Lord was against the Philistines all the days of Samuel.
And Samuel judged Israel all the days of his life.
And he went from year to year in circuit to Beth–el, and Gilgal, and Mizpeh, and judged Israel in all those places.
And his return was to Ramah; for there was his house; and there he judged Israel; and there he built an altar unto the Lord.
And some days after Paul said unto Barnabas, Let us go again and visit our brethren in every city where we have preached the word of the Lord, and see how they do.
Samuel, the prophet of the Lord, beloved of his Lord, established a kingdom, and anointed princes over his people.
By the law of the Lord he judged the congregation, and the Lord had respect unto Jacob.
By his faithfulness he was found a true prophet, and by his word he was known to be faithful in vision.
For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.

And Samuel spake unto all the house of Israel, saying, If ye do return unto the Lord with all your hearts, then put away the strange gods and Ashtaroth from among you, and prepare your hearts unto the Lord, and serve him only: and he will deliver you out of the hand of the Philistines.
Then the children of Israel did put away Baalim and Ashtaroth, and served the Lord only.
